item.title: CAR-T expertise draws foreign cancer patients
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
A Romanian patient with a serious form of lymphoma, a type of blood cancer that had returned despite previous treatment, has been discharged from Shanghai Tongji Hospital after receiving an advanced cancer treatment administered by a Chinese medical team. The 58-year-old woman, Sandica-Iuliana Klein, came to Shanghai specifically for treatment this summer. Doctors said she was the hospital's first Romanian patient and may also be the first Romanian to travel to China for CAR-T therapy, an advanced treatment that uses a patient's own immune cells to fight cancer. CAR-T therapy involves collecting immune cells called T cells from a patient's blood, modifying them in a laboratory to help them recognize and attack cancer cells, and then returning them to the patient's body. The treatment essentially equips the body's natural defense system with a more targeted ability to fight tumors. Klein underwent a combination of radiotherapy and CAR-T therapy at the Shanghai hospital. By the time she was discharged, her levels of lactate dehydrogenase, an enzyme in the blood that can indicate the extent of tumor activity, had fallen significantly, suggesting a positive response to treatment. Klein had previously received treatment for lymphoma in Romania and achieved remission, meaning the signs of cancer had disappeared. However, the disease progressed again last year. Further chemotherapy in Romania brought only partial remission, with some cancer remaining. With CAR-T treatment unavailable in her home country, long waiting times in many other countries and relatively few hospitals in Europe offering comprehensive treatment, Klein and her family began looking overseas. They eventually focused on China after learning about Tongji Hospital's experience in CAR-T therapy and its successful treatment of international patients. Through an online medical consultation, they contacted the team led by Li Ping, a professor in the hospital's hematology department. Klein arrived in Shanghai on Aug 22, and her T cells were collected six days later. Li said that she also had scleroderma, a rare condition that causes the skin to become hard and tight, as well as hypothyroidism, in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough hormones to regulate functions such as metabolism. "Using CAR-T treatment for her was like killing multiple birds with one stone, and it really saved her life," Li said. The medical team conducted additional genetic tests and found a mutation that placed Klein at a higher risk of the cancer returning. To reduce that risk, doctors arranged radiotherapy before reinfusing her modified T cells. The aim was to shrink the tumor first, making the subsequent CAR-T treatment more effective and reducing the likelihood of relapse, Li said. "Often the challenge with CAR-T lies not in the reinfusion itself but in the comprehensive management before and after the infusion," she said, emphasizing the importance of careful preparation and follow-up. Klein, whose husband is from the United States, said patients in her home country usually consider seeking advanced treatment in North America. However, she decided on China after comparing treatment costs and medical experience. CAR-T treatment in China costs about one-third of the price in the US, while Chinese hospitals also have extensive experience in administering the therapy, she said. Tongji Hospital was among the first hospitals in China to conduct clinical research on CAR-T therapy, beginning in 2015. The hospital has since treated more than 1,000 patients. More than 100 patients from foreign countries and regions, including Thailand and Singapore, have traveled to the Shanghai hospital specifically for the treatment. "What surprised me the most was how international this hospital is. From the first video call with Professor Li, I felt I could entrust myself to this team. They are professional and gentle, explaining every step clearly, even those test results I failed to understand," Klein said. Following her discharge, Li's team will conduct monthly remote follow-ups for six months and coordinate with hospitals in Romania to arrange further care.

item.title: Shenzhou XXIV crew enters China's Tiangong space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
JIUQUAN -- The Shenzhou XXIV crew, comprising Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, entered China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday. Serving as a payload specialist, Ali has made history by becoming the first foreigner to board Tiangong. The astronaut trio took off at 8:18 am (Beijing Time) the same day aboard China's Shenzhou XXIV spaceship from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Northwest China. The Shenzhou XXIII crew in orbit opened the hatch of the space station at 2:35 pm and welcomed the new arrivals, according to the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA). After entering the space station, the Shenzhou XXIV crew met with the three Shenzhou XXIII astronauts, who have been in orbit for about six months. The two crews then took group pictures of the ninth space get-together in China's aerospace history. They will now start a new in-orbit handover round. Ali will join in the crew's routine work and focus on joint China-Pakistan space science experiments while in orbit, primarily installing experiment samples and units, and carrying out in-orbit experiments, CMSA spokesman Zhang Jingbo revealed at a news conference on Tuesday. After completing a short-term joint flight, Ali will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou XXIII spacecraft alongside two Shenzhou XXIII crew members. The other two Shenzhou XXIV astronauts will stay in orbit for roughly six months along with Shenzhou XXIII astronaut Zhu Yangzhu, who has already spent six months in orbit and will remain aboard Tiangong to complete a year-long stay experiment.

item.title: Nation's opening-up fuels growth across Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
China's deepening opening-up and strengthening focus on innovation, advanced manufacturing and green technology are creating new development opportunities across the Asia-Pacific region, business leaders said. Those opportunities are increasingly flowing in both directions as regional markets become more integrated, said Rose Zhu, chief country officer of Deutsche Bank China. "For multinational companies, China remains an important market, innovation hub and part of global supply chains," Zhu said. "We see particularly strong potential along key growth corridors connecting China with other (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) economies, Europe and the Middle East." At the same time, Chinese companies are increasingly looking overseas to diversify their markets, expand their global footprint and participate more deeply in international value chains, she said. Alan Li, president of CBRE China, said, "Multinationals are no longer chasing low costs." Instead, they are seeking to tap China's advanced technology, talent pool and consumer market, while benefiting from a more open and unified business environment, he said. New office leasing by foreign companies in major Chinese cities rose 26 percent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, the strongest increase since 2022, according to CBRE, a commercial real estate services and investment company headquartered in the United States. Demand was led by financial and professional services, up 31 percent, and consumer-sector companies, up 34 percent. China's supply-chain strengths and talent base have continued to attract investment in advanced manufacturing, particularly in life sciences, advanced equipment and new energy vehicle components, Li said. For multinational manufacturers, China's advantage increasingly lies in the speed at which technology can transition from development to commercial application. "China's strong industrial ecosystem and diverse application scenarios help accelerate testing and adoption at scale," said Hendrik Kohleick, president of Henkel Asia-Pacific. Fast-growing sectors including electric mobility, artificial intelligence, humanoid robotics and data centers are creating demand for new materials and industrial processes that improve performance, efficiency and sustainability, while consumers are seeking more personalized, high-quality and sustainable products, he said. Henkel, a German multinational chemical and consumer goods company, sees China as both a market and an innovation hub, Kohleick said. Its local research, manufacturing and technical-service capabilities allow solutions developed and validated in China to be deployed through regional networks, serving markets across the Asia-Pacific region with consistent quality and speed, he added. For APEC economies with abundant renewable energy resources, Chinese technology and capital can help convert those resources into local economic opportunities, from electric vehicle supply chains to renewable power projects and data centers. Fonterra, a New Zealand dairy cooperative owned by farmers, provides an example of how such industry links can support the low-carbon transition. Teh-han Chow, CEO of Fonterra China, said that a China-made electric boiler installed at Fonterra's Edendale site in New Zealand had replaced coal-fired equipment, reducing the emissions from milk processing. This project shows how cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region can draw on complementary strengths to accelerate the transition to a low-carbon economy while maintaining reliable and efficient production, he said.

item.title: Azerbaijan official: GDI offers timely answers to common challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
In an exclusive interview with China Daily, Elchin Amirbayov, special representative of President Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan, stated that the Global Development Initiative (GDI) is important and timely. During his visit to China from Nov 16 to 20 at the invitation of the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, he said that amid multiple challenges, including geopolitical turbulence, development imbalances, and climate change, the GDI places development at the core of the global agenda and offers equal development opportunities for all countries. Amirbayov welcomed Chinese enterprises to Azerbaijan to take part in bilateral cooperation in areas such as renewable energy and to help turn the UN Sustainable Development Goals from blueprints into reality. item.title: From punk to rap, women upend cliches
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
"Yesterday, another one of my girlfriends died. The day before, we were still blaming her for not being there, saying we couldn't get a full table of mahjong without her. One by one, they've all gone … I'm terribly afraid of dying." The words are delivered in a strong regional accent over a rap beat by a woman in her 60s. There is no cool music video, choreographed performance or manufactured hip-hop image. Instead, she speaks openly about death, friendship and the people disappearing from her life. The song, Yesterday, Another One of My Girlfriends Died, is the work of Gui Xiang, a 62-year-old woman from Suzhou, Jiangsu province, who has found an unlikely fan base through rap. Her unconventional performances are growing in popularity on Chinese social media, where her age, raw delivery, accent and irreverent humor defy images usually associated with hip-hop artists. She has 215,000 followers on Xiaohongshu (Red-Note) and 575,000 on Douyin, where her videos have accumulated more than 12.35 million likes. Gui is part of a growing cohort of middle-aged and older Chinese women indulging in unexpected musical roles, from rappers and rock musicians to singers who have turned public parks into their stages. Their stories point to a broader shift in how some Chinese women are approaching later stages of life. Instead of restricting their leisure activities to familiar pursuits, such as square dancing in public parks, practicing tai chi or doing morning exercises and looking after grandchildren, they are experimenting with fresh artistic expression, including genres and subcultures traditionally associated with younger people. A growing interest in tech skills and an appetite for late-life learning are also improving their capabilities to pursue new interests. The 2025 New Silver Generation Lifestyle Report, published by Beijing News, found that more than half of the respondents — those aged over 60 — had attended or were attending interest classes or training courses. Nearly one-fifth were learning new skills, ranging from using digital devices and photography to handicrafts and short-video editing. The report also found that short-video platforms have become an important part of older people's lives, with nearly 60 percent of respondents using platforms such as Douyin and Kuaishou. Sociologist Zhang Hexuan, who holds a doctorate from University College London, said this generation is entering old age equipped with new digital tools and skills. They have diverse sources of information and a strong desire to explore, he said, while retaining a preference for social interaction and collective activities. "Personal growth and a sense of belonging to a group are developing simultaneously in this generation," he said. China's community networks provide a foundation for the more varied, multi-interest lifestyles they are seeking, Zhang added.

item.title: Weekly train service linking China, Mongolia and Russia launched
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
A passenger train departed Beijing for Irkutsk, Russia, on Wednesday morning, marking the launch of a weekly rail service linking China, Mongolia and Russia. The V3 train left Beijing Railway Station at 7:27 am and is scheduled to arrive in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, on Thursday afternoon before reaching Irkutsk on Friday afternoon. The 2,666-kilometer journey takes about 55 hours. The train stops at cities and towns in all three countries, including Jining and Ereenhot in China, Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia and Ulan-Ude in Russia.

item.description:

The Shenzhou XXIV crewed spaceship blasted off from Jiuquan on Wednesday morning and successfully entered orbit, carrying Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to China's Tiangong space station. The mission marks the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program, and the first time a foreign astronaut has visited the Tiangong space station. item.title: Xi, Pakistani president exchange congratulations over joint spaceflight mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING -- President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries. It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission. In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese Shenzhou spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to inhabit China's space station. Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people. Xi noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago. Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation, and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity. For his part, Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people. He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship, and promote the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries to a higher level.

item.title: Cook Islands scientist joins historic deep-sea dive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
A scientist from the Cook Islands has become the first person from her country to directly observe the deep-sea seabed within its exclusive economic zone, joining a dive aboard China's manned submersible Jiaolong in the Manihiki fracture zone on Nov 21 local time, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on Tuesday. Chloe Wragg joined Chinese scientists Yang Yifan and Zhao Shengya aboard the submersible to conduct an environmental survey. The mission successfully achieved its objectives, collecting valuable deep-sea environmental data and samples. The successful dive highlights the blue partnership between China and the Cook Islands and further strengthens their cooperation in deep-sea science and technology, the ministry said. Following the dive, Wragg expressed her excitement at witnessing the milestone firsthand. She said the Cook Islands has long been at the forefront of deep-sea scientific research and that the dive demonstrated the country's determination and commitment to deepening its understanding of its own seabed. She also expressed her gratitude for the opportunity to work with colleagues from the National Deep Sea Center and the Second Institute of Oceanography, both under the Ministry of Natural Resources. Wragg said the expedition reflected the longstanding friendship and scientific ties between the two countries, as well as their close relations and extensive exchanges. The expedition marks the second joint marine scientific mission between China and the Cook Islands, following their first such mission in 2025. During the current expedition, Jiaolong is scheduled to conduct five dives in the Cook Islands' exclusive economic zone. The mission aims to help the country fill gaps in its basic deep-sea data and train its first group of local researchers in crewed submersible operations through hands-on experience.
